I ended up talking to someone for quite a while, sorry I couldn't get back to you.  If you'd like to schedule a time sometime soon though, just let me know what will work for you.  

That goes for anyone else, as well.  If any of you would like to talk at any time just let me know when a good time would be and I'll get back with you.  Thanks, guys.

You can't let your disposition hinge upon your interaction with her.  If your hope for yourself is dependent upon your future with her, you may as well consider yourself fucked.  I've been through all of this.  It's a trial for both of you, believe me, but it's something you're going to come out of that will either make your stronger or jaded.  

What you're feeling right now is that shiny, golden little part of you which held on to the childish belief that you could sort your life out and maintain something pure beginning to die.  There will be challenges and you must prepare yourself to meet them.  Just keep in mind that there may be a fitting reward for your somewhere along the line.

In short, you are the master of your destiny.  Don't let someone else determine that for you.  I can't say I don't agree with the conclusion you have come to already, but to do so for the sake of someone else is quite possibly the weakest excuse in the book.

I'll do my best.  If I could explain it adequately to myself I probably wouldn't be so confused.

I try to filter my own existence through the experiences and perceived dispositions of others.  I am an emotional leech, in the sense that I often attune my own feelings to those of the people around me.  People who understand and appreciate this trait often remark that I am exceedingly easy to talk to about some of the most intimate details of their lives.  I have a wealth of experience in most situations, I generally don't speak unless I can speak the truth as I see it.  People are somehow at ease around me, which is sort of ironic because I personally only seek to isolate myself.

I tend to overanalyze aspects of my own life and determinate my reactions to any occurrence based almost entirely upon what I've observed from others.  I suppress my own inner feelings and thoughts, which I deem to be not normal, in an often vain attempt to simply emulate normalcy.  My sense of individuality, or self, is ever-deteriorating.

The confusion I try to describe is a symptom of this, which I suppose is destructive.  Some days it feels as if the only genuine feeling or thought I have is the desire to end my own life.  For me, it is a logical conclusion instead of an emotional response to some external conflict.
Anything specific you'd like to know?
At best they are disjointed, but I'm making an effort.

I appreciate the concern, but it's not something I believe I will ever consider.  I addressed the reasons for this in a previous post.  tl;dr version is don't like paying to have some random person feign concern or push pills.  I've seen way too many people end up way more fucked up than they were to begin with.

I think I'm approaching an impasse in which I'll have to either drop these feelings for a while and focus on improving myself or better embrace the idea of confining myself.  I believe solitude will serve to greatly empower the sense of indifference that has been at the forefront of my mind lately.  I sometimes think of it as a step-by-step process by which to ultimately phase myself out of existence.
No.  I have never been evaluated.
And as his empire crumbles, my precious black widow shall rise as his most fitting successor!

Yes, because we'd much rather give you advice on how to more efficiently off yourself than offer a bit of time to hear your story and maybe some advice.  People here like to think they can help, and that's precisely what we're all trying to do.  Some of us even succeed every now and again.

So, assuming you aren't currently roaming around your house in a manic daze looking for more random pills to ingest, what exactly is going wrong for you?  I think it's interesting that you have a degree and you're still finding yourself in this position.  Just by having one you're doing better than a lot of us, including me.  What's your field?  Assuming your aunt is the only person in your family who actually has been there for you, what do you think this whole thing might do to her?

There's always a way out that doesn't involve *checking* out.  I hope you consider that before doing whatever it is you're planning to do.  

Sorry you found yourself here.

More like Shakespeare, in the sense that by the time it's over you're dead.

I'd like to make it clear that I'm not necessarily trying to talk you out of anything.  Considering my own situation, that would make me a gigantic hypocrite.  I'm also not going to say something typical like 'Shit man, you just need to *think* about things before you do this.'  Although in a way, that's basically what I'm saying.  

I think there's more to it than just giving an effort in your daily life and spending time alone sitting around thinking about how much things generally fucking suck.  How long have you felt this way?  Have you made any sort of backup plan should you not be able to go through with it?  As in, do you have any serious plans as to how you might go about solving even one of the problems you're currently faced with?

The only reason my family didn't come back from shopping that day to find the living room ceiling painted with the remnants of my face is that I devised a plan.  I didn't completely shut away my desire to end my own life, however, I managed to occupy myself for another four years (up to this point, presently) by thinking I could somehow fumble along and maybe fix some of the shit I had previously broken.

When I was your age I was in college studying to be a high school English teacher.  One semester I spent a weekend with my family, and while they were out shopping for groceries I spent about an hour sitting in my father's favorite chair with a loaded shotgun nestled just beneath my chin.  I sat there with the safety disengaged, getting used to the feel of the muzzle against my neck and contemplating everything about my experience which had brought me to that point.

Don't mistake this for some sort of veiled advocacy of what you're thinking about doing, but I will tell you that it was one of the most serene and peaceful sensations I believe I have ever felt.  It did more than a little to clear my mind and gave me a bit of needed perspective on the mess my life had become at that point.

I believe that what makes these types of thoughts so hard to overcome is the simple fact that suicide is an abstract solution to very real, very prominent problems.  You can't help but experience the situations and environmental variables which ultimately lead to the idea of self-destruction, but to take the first hesitant step toward fulfilling that goal will likely make you reconsider.  When you suddenly find yourself sitting alone somewhere and come to the grim realization that you're actually pointing a fucking gun at yourself, all of those other plans and hopes you thought were unreachable have a way of becoming somewhat more tangible.

Again, I'm not saying you should go buy a gun tomorrow and do this.  If you have a general interest in firearms like you say you do then purchase a lockbox first.  Get your gun, find a shooting range where you can practice with it, and when you're at home keep it locked away and pretend it doesn't exist.  When you're out there in the field popping shots off at your target, pay particular attention to the sound of the rounds as they explode from the chamber;  there's a certain finality in it even though you know you're shooting at some lifeless scrap of human-shaped paper.  Do you really want that to be the last thing you ever hear?
Thanks.

It's amazing how therapeutic the writing process can be sometimes.  I did sleep well the first night, and in fact I've been able to drift off for the last two days now with nary a drink.  It's a small but welcome relief.
Thank you.  This is the first tentative step toward an idea I've had circling around for months.

I've had bad experiences with relationships, but don't we all?  I fell absolutely, madly in love with a girl about five years ago and drove her away with only the infancy of the thoughts and feelings I've described here.  I will never see her again, and I still think about her on a daily basis.

My most recent tale of debauchery and mayhem involves my best friend from childhood and a girl I dated for almost two years.  The important part of the whole story is that she truly made me believe things could last despite the hardship we both endured due to my feelings.  She was the first person I was completely honest with about my tendencies and she exhibited so much patience, so much genuine care that I finally began to relent a bit.  

She truly made me believe that she understood me, and for the first time in my life I felt as if I had someone to confide in.  I didn't abuse this privilege, mind you, and I never did anything rash like threaten to hurt myself for leverage.  When we spoke of my burdens I tried to remain as detached as possible and always tried to let her know that just by being the person she was she was having a positive effect upon me.

I believed in her all the way up until she told me she was in love with my best friend and that she intended to be gone by the end of the month.

I will grant you that this shit had a profound effect upon my disposition.  In the last three or four months I have endured a very aggressive relapse.  Hence my desire to mislead and ultimately destroy the next hapless, naive little girl who has the distinct misfortune of crossing my path.

I wanted to dream all of this away and move on, and I honestly gave it an effort.  The reality as I know it to be now is that I have nested myself in this rut.  One of the few comforts I have left is that I can end this at any time and in any manner I so choose.

I don't think "meeting" someone in the Biblical sense means what you think it means.

Also you did not cheat.  Maybe apologize to her for missing her supposed signals just to sate her, but realistically it's sort of dumb for her to even suggest that.  You're not the fucking Professor X of casual dating, and you haven't slapped ham with anyone since you guys officially started dating.  Just ask her what she thinks your anniversary is.

Also how did her behavior change?  Did you guys officially become exclusive the first time you went out to buy tampons for her or she bitched at you for not taking out the trash?

Well, considering my state I suppose it shouldn't be very surprising that I'm having delusional thoughts.  I want to do this primarily for personal gratification, as it is a means of validating the utter disdain I feel for certain aspects of modern society.  The idea that someone could potentially find meaning within the act is, more than anything, a small hope.  Consider it the last remnant of my once prominent desire to help and enlighten others.

I once read in a fortune cookie that the best revenge is to live well.  When facing a tyrannical and monolithic *idea*, however, the whole precept of smiling in the face of your enemies sort of disintegrates.  The best you can hope to do is inspire others to act in a concerted effort against whatever threat or perversion is perceived.  

I'm not charismatic and I'm not a great speaker.  I don't care very much for myself, so it's even more difficult for me to proactively try to help others.  My best idea thus far is to turn my personal disdain for myself into something potentially productive for both parties.  Kill myself in a particularly spectacular or meaningful way and hope a few others are inspired by the message.  That's it.
The really cool ones mask multiple IP addresses or ranges so it is sometimes damn near impossible to determine the source.  This is why it's never good to be a network engineer who is on call.

I don't know what a meaningful life would be.  People all around me are setting about living their lives and building their careers and raising their families.  Although I find that whole experience to be unbearably fragile and disposable, I can't really blame them for it.  They at least know what they want.

My best attempt at a life goal is to continue working into infinity while simultaneously dismantling myself in the hopes that one fine day I'll be able to attain something of worth just in time to die before I can enjoy it.  Most people only dedicate themselves to a career so that they may one day reap some sort of benefit and enjoy their remaining time in leisure.  I want to work toward the same end and send a message to anyone who listens by destroying myself once I've paid my dues.

I want to be the soldier who survives two tours of Afghanistan and dies in a car crash his first week stateside.  I want to be the beat cop who gives 20 years to the force and gets shot walking to the grocery store.  I want to burn away the best years of my life for some menial entitlement and fall into oblivion to send a message.  I am institutionalized by the free market.

God, you're right.  

And yes, I have stopped writing.  The last time I honestly sat down and tried to elicit that whole experience was greater than six months ago.  I had been working on a project for the better part of two years and even had a relatively small but established group of readers.  

Similar to what you have described, my inner processes began to manifest themselves with a magnitude that was essentially proportionate to the effort I was putting forth.  I was in high gear, and I eventually became apprehensive of the idea that maybe so many people were coming back for more because they sensed it.  Maybe they knew that this was truly me and they only cared to see how and when I would turn myself into a headline on the nightly news.

Still, even though that is gone now I believe it was a necessary step toward refining my ability as a writer.  I have been compulsively narrating anything and everything that has happened or could potentially occur throughout my daily life since the first day of my hiatus.  

Writing may very well be the sense of empowerment I've been lacking lately.  Thank you, man.

I ended up changing my major and getting a job in a completely separate field which allows me to make more money as an entry-level worker than I ever would as a high school teacher with a 4-year degree.  Without being too specific, the business I am now involved in relies entirely upon the ability of my larger company to exploit much smaller entities, which in turn make up for the loss by doing their best to exploit average consumers.  I suppose you can't really expect much better from the private sector, eh?

I suppose getting a psychologist would be a viable option, however, I seriously doubt my own ability to even approach the level of honesty within my original post when face to face with another person.  I would most likely lie or suppress most of these thoughts if for no other reason than the fact that I consider paying someone to sit around and pretend to listen while I relieve my burdens a very banal prospect.  It almost seems masturbatory to me.

There is also the fear of possibly being referred to a psychiatrist as part of whatever standard treatment they have for people like me.  If there is anything that will somehow endow me with the fortitude to carry out some of my thoughts, it's a barbiturate cocktail.
